title: भाषा शिक्षकका दृष्टिकोणमा सुनाइ सिप परीक्षण {Listening skills test from a language teacher's point of view}
nepali: कथ्य वा विद्युतीय सामग्रीमा व्यक्त भाव, विषयवस्तु, सन्देश, सूचना, तथ्य वा अनुभव बुझ्ने गरी सुन्नुलाई सुनाइ सिप भनिन्छ । उपर्य‘क्त पक्षको प्राप्ति भए नभएको मापन वा लेखाजोखा गर्नु नै सुनाइ सिप परीक्षण हो । सुनाइ सिप परीक्षणबारे भाषा शिक्षकको दृष्टिकोण पहिचान गर्ने उद्देश्यले यो लेख तयार पारिएको छ । पूर्वकार्यको समीक्षालाई आधार मान्दा नेपालमा प्रयोगात्मक मूल्याङ्कनको सन्दर्भमा सुनाइ सिप परीक्षणको व्यवस्था भए पनि यसको कार्यान्वयनका विषयमा अध्ययन भएको देखिँदैन । सर्वेक्षण विधिको प्रयोग गरी ४१ जना शिक्षकबाट मतावली लिई परिमाणात्मक ढाँचामा यस अध्ययनलाई पूरा गरिएको छ । सुनाइ सिप परीक्षण सम्बन्धी कथन निर्माण गरी लिकर्ट पद्धतिबाट विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । पाँचओटा स्केलमा दृष्टिकोण लिई प्रतिशतमार्फत परिणामको छलफल गरी निष्कर्षमा पुगिएको छ । माध्यमिक तहमा सुनाइ सिप परीक्षणमा शिक्षकहरू सचेत भए पनि यसको प्रयोग र व्यवहारमा सैद्धान्तिक दृष्टिले एकरूपता हुन नसकेको देखिन्छ । प्रयोगात्मक मूल्याङ्कनमार्फत सुनाइ र बोलाइ सिपको परीक्षण गर्ने व्यवस्था प्रशंसनीय भए पनि यसको साधन र परीक्षण पद्धतिमा निश्चित मार्गदर्शन हुन सकेको देखिएन । सुनाइ सिप परीक्षण गर्दा मौखिक अभिव्यक्तिबाट तथा श्रुतिलेखन र श्रुतिबोधलाई मुख्य आधार मान्नुपर्ने तथ्यबाट पुष्टि भएको छ । श्रव्य सामग्रीको उचित व्यवस्थापनका साथ वस्तुगत प्रश्नबाटविद्यार्थीको सुनाइ सिप परीक्षण गरिएको छ । यस लेखबाट प्राप्त तथ्यले पाठ्यक्रम निर्माता,पाठ्यपुस्तक लेखक, भाषा शिक्षक तथा शिक्षण सिकाइसँग सरोकार राखी नवप्रवर्तनप्रति चासो दिने सम्पूर्ण व्यक्तिलाई सहयोग पुग्दछ ।
american_english: Listening so as to understand the thoughts, subject matter, message, information, facts, or experience expressed in spoken or electronic material is called listening skill. Measuring or assessing whether the above aspects have been acquired is what listening skills testing is. This article has been prepared with the objective of identifying language teachers' perspectives on listening skills testing. Taking the review of prior work as a basis, although provision for listening skills testing exists in the context of practical assessment in Nepal, no study appears to have been conducted on its implementation. Using the survey method, this study was completed in a quantitative format by taking opinions from 41 teachers. Statements related to listening skills testing were constructed and analyzed using the Likert method. Perspectives were taken on five scales and, through percentages, the results were discussed and conclusions reached. Although teachers are aware of listening skills testing at the secondary level, theoretical uniformity could not be achieved in its use and practice. Although the arrangement of testing listening and speaking skills through practical assessment is praiseworthy, definite guidance could not be established in its tools and testing method. It has been confirmed by the fact that, when testing listening skills, oral expression as well as dictation and listening comprehension should be taken as the main basis. With appropriate management of audio material, students' listening skills have been tested through objective questions. The facts obtained from this article help curriculum developers, textbook authors, language teachers, and all individuals concerned with teaching and learning who take an interest in innovation.

informal_english: Listening so you actually understand the thoughts, subject matter, message, info, facts, or experience in spoken or electronic stuff is what we call listening skill. Checking whether you've actually picked up those aspects is what listening skills testing is. This piece was written to figure out what language teachers think about listening skills testing. Based on a review of prior work, Nepal does have listening skills testing in practical assessment, but nobody seems to have studied how it's actually implemented. Using a survey, this study was done quantitatively with opinions from 41 teachers. Statements about listening skills testing were built and analyzed with the Likert method. Perspectives were taken on five scales and, through percentages, the results were talked through and conclusions reached. Even though secondary teachers are aware of listening skills testing, it couldn't be made theoretically consistent in actual use and practice. Testing listening and speaking through practical assessment is a great idea, but there's no clear guidance on the tools and methods. It checks out that when testing listening skills, you've really got to use oral expression, dictation, and listening comprehension as the main basis. With audio material handled properly, students' listening skills were tested with objective questions. The findings here should help curriculum developers, textbook authors, language teachers, and anyone interested in teaching and learning who cares about innovation.
